title: Accelerometry-Derived Digital Biomarkers for Cardiometabolic Risk: A Population-Representative Tabular Benchmark with Uncertainty Quantification
summary: The paper introduces a population-representative NHANES 2003–2006 tabular benchmark (N=1,381) linking hip-worn accelerometry and lifestyle covariates to HbA1c, triglycerides, and CRP, with subgroup evaluation and conformal uncertainty. It compares ridge, XGBoost, and TabPFN v2 on a single 60/20/20 stratified split and applies split conformal prediction at 90% coverage. TabPFN v2 gives the best point predictions, most clearly for CRP (R2=0.383), while triglycerides remain nearly unpredictable and subgroup coverage reveals fairness gaps.

match_target.why: This is the user's target and the paper's headline result: TabPFN v2 CRP R2=0.383 has the largest model margin and requires only one small tabular fit plus test evaluation, making it the cheapest claim that still demonstrates the central finding.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: R^2 is a bounded score printed as a fraction in [0,1] on a test set of N=276 (<2,000), and the paper reports no std over repeated runs; the band is therefore 0.02 absolute.

requirements.stmt: Use NHANES 2003–2006 cycles C and D and restrict to participants with valid hip-worn accelerometry: at least 4 wear days and at least 600 min/day wear time.
requirements.quote: Starting from participants with valid accelerometry data (≥4 wear days, ≥600 min/day wear time)

requirements.stmt: Apply inclusion criteria: age 20–85 years, non-missing HbA1c, triglycerides, and CRP, and fasting duration at least 8 hours before blood draw; target final N=1,381.
requirements.quote: age 20–85 years; non-missing HbA1c, triglycerides, and CRP; and fasting duration ≥8 hours prior to blood draw

requirements.stmt: Construct the six accelerometry features: TAC, log-TAC, sedentary time, MVPA, light PA, and wear time from minute-level accelerometry with standard Troiano cutpoints.
requirements.quote: Activity features (6): total activity counts (TAC), log-TAC (TLAC), sedentary time (ST), moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA), light PA (LIPA), and wear time (WT)

requirements.stmt: Construct the 12 demographic/clinical covariates: age, sex, race/ethnicity, poverty-income ratio, BMI, systolic blood pressure, smoking status, and energy, carbohydrate, fat, protein, and fibre intake.
requirements.quote: age, sex, race/ethnicity, poverty-income ratio, BMI, systolic blood pressure, smoking status, and total energy, carbohydrate, fat, protein, and fibre intake

requirements.stmt: Use a single stratified random 60/20/20 train/calibration/test split with seed=42; the test set should be N=276.
requirements.quote: train (60%), calibration (20%), and test (20%) sets using stratified random splitting (seed=42)

requirements.stmt: Standardize numerical features using training-set statistics and label-encode sex, race/ethnicity, and smoking status.
requirements.quote: Numerical features were standardised using training-set statistics. Categorical features (sex, race/ethnicity, smoking) were label-encoded.

requirements.stmt: Log-transform all three outcomes before modelling; compute reported R2 and MAE on the log scale.
requirements.quote: All outcomes were log-transformed prior to modelling to address right-skewed distributions; reported metrics are computed on the log scale.

requirements.stmt: Fit ridge regression with alpha=1.0 as the linear baseline.
requirements.quote: Ridge Regression (α=1.0): a linear specialised baseline providing an interpretable lower bound on predictive performance.

requirements.stmt: Fit XGBoost with 500 estimators, learning rate 0.05, max depth 6, and early stopping on the calibration set.
requirements.quote: We used 500 estimators with learning rate 0.05, max depth 6, and early stopping on the calibration set.

requirements.stmt: Use TabPFN v2 without task-specific gradient training: pass training examples directly as in-context examples and do not subsample when Ntrain=828 (<1,000). Use CPU inference.
requirements.quote: training instances are passed directly as in-context examples, with subsampling to 1,000 examples applied only when the training set exceeds this size

requirements.stmt: Apply split conformal prediction per model and outcome using absolute calibration residuals and alpha=0.10, producing intervals yhat ± qhat.
requirements.quote: For each model and outcome, we computed the non-conformity score as the absolute residual |yi −ˆyi| on the calibration set

requirements.stmt: Report R2, MAE on the log scale, and empirical conformal coverage for every model–outcome combination on the test set.
requirements.quote: Table 2 reports R2, mean absolute error (MAE, log scale), and empirical conformal coverage

requirements.stmt: Evaluate subgroup conformal coverage by sex and race/ethnicity, including Mexican American, Other Hispanic, Non-Hispanic White, Non-Hispanic Black, and Other.
requirements.quote: using the NHANES oversampling design that ensures adequate representation of minority groups

data.name: NHANES 2003–2004 (cycle C) and 2005–2006 (cycle D) public-use files
data.how_to_get: Download demographics, examination, laboratory, questionnaire, dietary, and accelerometry (PAXRAW_C/PAXRAW_D) files from the CDC/NCHS NHANES website: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/

data.name: NHANES Accelerometry Cardiometabolic Benchmark derived dataset
data.how_to_get: Public repository linked by the paper: https://github.com/felizzi/nhanes-accel-cardiometabolic-benchmark

data.name: TabPFN v2 model/package
data.how_to_get: Install the official TabPFN implementation and use the v2 checkpoint; the paper cites Hollmann et al. (2025) and does not provide a separate URL.
